labeler: AI agent (Claude), not a lawyer; single labeler, no second-rater agreement measured

precision.sampling: stratified by rule_id: every detection for rules with <=10 detections, else max(10, ceil(8%)) drawn uniformly at random (Python random.Random(20261022).sample)
precision.note: SE is ~0 because every sampled stratum was either all-true or fully enumerated; it reflects sampling only, not labeler error. The Wilson-lower figure weights each rule's 95% lower bound by its population and is the conservative number to quote.

span_accuracy.convention: exact = from first character of the citation (case name if present; signal excluded) through the last element of the citation (pincite, subsection, date/court parenthetical for cases; explanatory parentheticals excluded). Statutes/regulations: code name through the full section, subsections and all listed sections; trailing (West 2024)/(2018) parentheticals not required.

recall.method: For each opinion the full text was rendered with every detection span marked inline and read end to end by the agent. Every citation the agent recognised that was not covered by any detection was recorded. A broad regex pass (an uncommitted helper script) listed citation-like strings outside detection spans as a cross-check; each listed candidate was confirmed by reading. Running page headers/footers (repeated captions, 'Cite as:' heads, 'Case: N Document: N Page: N' furniture) are excluded from both detected and missed counts. Borderline references (bare 'Rule 8' / 'section 13-116' in prose, named acts without a cite, dictionaries, patents by number, URLs) are listed but not counted.

docs.note: the regex pass listed 120 uncovered strings, all confirmed by reading; 4 more were found by reading only
